analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (TransitionWatchdogTests.swift, AutopilotTinyModelTests.swift, and an assertion added to ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift near line 683). No production source is changed in the supplied evidence, so this diff adds no attack surface, auth, crypto or data-exposure changes, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated.

The tests exercise a transition watchdog and autopilot lease behavior whose implementation is outside this batch. Behaviors they encode:
- Stalls are bounded at 600s or 300s.
- A stalled startup preload is stopped before its next model without interrupting the in-flight load.
- A stalled autopilot operation fails as transition_stalled and releases its load and KV reservation.
- Without consent the watchdog neither acts nor reports.
- Inventory adoption survives the lease until an admin unload.
- Failed or no-room operations place nothing.
- A held inventory model idles out only after its hold expires.

The ProviderModelSwitchTests assertion checks that the .modelSwitch busy reason is released on failure and that .draining stays set only on an unconfirmed commit, which is consistent with fail-closed admission.

The tests use testing-only hooks, such as startupPreloadTask injection and the busy-flag setters, via @testable import. These are in the test target and not production surface.

Remaining question for integration: the production watchdog and supervision code is not in this batch. Whether it correctly handles consent gating, cancellation of other owners' load gates, and the interaction with T-010 (cancellation propagation), T-029 (idle GPU) and T-041 hold and TTL semantics cannot be verified here. Tiny-model tests use temporary model caches and the existing prefix-cache fixtures. They do not alter the T-041 at-rest posture.
